text:
maria: ran a quick scaling sim for the admission controller, results surprising at 90% slot util
cheng: what surprised you?
kyle: can you paste the sim output?
maria: short version — TPM headroom goes negative when avg_seq_len spikes and KV hit drops below 30%
anya: that sounds like we're not adjusting for effective token cost per request
maria: exactly. current config uses tokens_per_request = avg_tokens. but with cache misses effective cost ~= avg_tokens * (1 + kv_miss_penalty)
cheng: propose we calculate Effective_Tokens = base_tokens * (1 + (1 - kv_hit_rate) * miss_factor)
maria: yes. miss_factor we measured ~0.45 on long-context workloads. so E = T * (1 + 0.45*(1-kv_hit))
kyle: can you show how that changes TPM budget?
maria: pasted sim snippet below (small table):
```
params: total_slots=128, tokens_per_sec_per_slot=40, avg_seq_len=120, kv_hit=0.25, miss_factor=0.45, safety=0.9
base_tokens_per_req = avg_seq_len = 120
E = 120 * (1 + 0.45*(1-0.25)) = 120 * (1 + 0.45*0.75) = 120 * 1.3375 = 160.5 tokens
slot_throughput_tokens_per_min = 40 * 60 = 2400 tokens/min per slot
cluster_throughput_tokens_per_min = 2400 * 128 = 307200 tokens/min
TPM_limit = cluster_throughput_tokens_per_min * safety / E = 307200 * 0.9 / 160.5 ≈ 1723 tpm
```
cheng: we currently advertise 2800 tpm for that pool — so we're oversubscribing by ~60% under those conditions
anya: wow. or in other words, high seq + low cache -> fewer requests handled than expected
sre-oncall: ops-bot, log current pool kv_hit rate and seq_len distribution for last 30m
ops-bot: scheduled query dispatched to telemetry. will post results when ready. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: simulation also shows smoothing burst credits helps but only up to 15% extra sustained tpm, beyond that latency SLOs spike
kyle: can we add a per-route multiplier to reduce offered TPM when recent kv_hit < 0.4? like route_tpm = advertised_tpm * (kv_hit * 0.7 + 0.3)
cheng: that's neat — soft gating. also consider short EWMA on avg_seq_len to catch sudden context-length shifts
anya: +1 on EWMA. maybe use alpha=0.2 and 3-min window
maria: added pseudo config to test:
```yaml
admission:
  safety_margin: 0.9
  evict_threshold: 0.95
  route_multipliers:
    default: 1.0
    long_context: 0.6 # applied when seq_len_ewma > 200 or kv_hit < 0.35
  seq_len_ewma_alpha: 0.2
  kv_hit_ewma_alpha: 0.25
```
ops-bot: telemetry query results: avg_kv_hit=0.28, p95_seq_len=310, avg_seq_len=145 over last 30m
sre-oncall: that matches the sim worst-case. we should reduce advertised tpm for that region's long-context routes now to avoid queueing backlog
kyle: I'll push a canary modifying route multiplier for the long-context tag to 0.5 for region-us-west-2 (5% traffic)
cheng: monitor latency tail and queue depth, roll back if p99 latency > 1200ms or queued requests > 300
maria: logging note: include effective_tokens in request traces. makes debugging admission decisions trivial
anya: also add per-gpu slot metric: "effective_tokens_consumed" so we can reconcile chargeback vs token counters
sre-oncall: +1. let's sync on a short runbook after canary deploy
maria: ok will draft and post shortly. thanks all :seedling:
